design.affected_system: fixed-route public transit service and passenger connections
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased transit-priority and timetable intervention
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased transit-priority and timetable intervention
pair route-level event-study with comparable untreated corridors with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Trips, stops, vehicle observations, disruptions, and calendars share a versioned service day.
Passenger loads and transfer behavior are measured or represented as bounded assumptions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased transit-priority and timetable intervention.

constraints.description: The transit reliability and passenger continuity evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: transit chief operating officer and service-planning director
design.decision_question: Did phased transit-priority and timetable changes improve reliable passenger travel without displacement?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The transit reliability and passenger continuity evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased transit-priority and timetable intervention passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: route-level event-study with comparable untreated corridors
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in passenger-weighted reliable travel time

design.intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased transit-priority and timetable intervention, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in passenger-weighted reliable travel time
distributional gap in change in passenger-weighted reliable travel time
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer causal passenger benefits from simple before-after vehicle speed.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased transit-priority and timetable intervention passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

design.title: Evaluate transit priority and schedule redesign
transportability_risks: Fare policy, headways, fleet, labor rules, topology, and passenger behavior vary by operator.
Reliability metrics may not transfer between schedule-based and frequency-based service.

family.affected_system: fixed-route public transit service and passenger connections
claim_boundary: Network, request, and schedule records do not establish individual travel behavior or harm.
Optimized routes and allocations are planning outputs, not dispatched or completed trips.
Design-only records do not claim current city data, implementation, compliance, or impact.
family.decision_owner: transit chief operating officer and service-planning director
family.description: Eight decisions covering reliability diagnosis, demand and delay forecasting, corridor investment, transfer siting, vehicle allocation, timetable design, disruption stress, and service-change evaluation.
family.title: Transit reliability and passenger continuity

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
